intro: Mati sits where the Pacific meets Mindanao — a coastline of skimboard breaks and sea-turtle sands, a bay of coral and dugongs, and a mountain range the world protects. Come feel it.

hero.subtitle: Pacific surf on one side of Mati, a protected bay of coral and dugongs on the other — and a short ride between them.

coasts.title: Surf, skim & sea turtles
coasts.blurb: Dahican's seven-kilometre crescent is where Mati earned its name as the skimboarding capital of the Philippines.

coasts.title: Islands, reefs & sunsets
coasts.blurb: Pujada Bay is a protected seascape — calm water, coral gardens, and island hops you can do in a morning.

attractions.name: Dahican Beach
attractions.tagline: Seven kilometres of Pacific white sand
attractions.blurb: Skimboarders at sunrise, surf through the amihan season, and sea-turtle nesting grounds watched over by the Amihan sa Dahican volunteers.
attractions.imageLabel: Drop a Dahican Beach photo — skimboarder at sunrise

sections.heading: Why go
sections.body: Dahican is the reason Mati calls itself the skimboarding capital of the Philippines. The long crescent faces the open Pacific, so mornings bring clean swell and a local scene of boards and bare feet at first light. It is also a protected nesting beach for marine turtles — the Amihan sa Dahican community group patrols the sands and helps release hatchlings.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Take a beginner skimboard or surf lesson from local instructors, walk the shoreline at sunrise, or simply settle in for the day. Ask the Amihan sa Dahican volunteers about turtle-conservation visits.

attractions.tagline: A mountain the world agreed to protect
attractions.blurb: Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List for its extraordinary biodiversity, from a pygmy forest of century-old bonsai to the Philippine eagle's range.

sections.heading: Why go
sections.body: Mount Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary is Davao Oriental's UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognised for a span of habitats packed into one mountain — including a celebrated pygmy forest where century-old trees grow only knee- to shoulder-high on mineral-rich soil. The range shelters a remarkable concentration of endemic and threatened plants and animals.

attractions.name: Pujada Bay
attractions.blurb: A protected seascape of coral reefs, dugongs and dolphins — with island hopping out to Pujada Island and quiet swimming coves.
attractions.where: Pujada Bay · west of the city

sections.heading: Why go
sections.body: Pujada Bay wraps the city in calm, clear water and is regularly named among the world's most beautiful bays. Beneath the surface are coral gardens and seagrass meadows that feed dugongs; pods of dolphins pass through the deeper channels.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Hire a local boat for island hopping to Pujada Island and the smaller islets, snorkel the reefs, or take a sunset cruise across the bay.

attractions.name: The Sleeping Dinosaur
attractions.tagline: The ridge the whole city knows by silhouette
attractions.blurb: The headland across the bay whose outline reads like a dinosaur at rest — best watched from the Baywalk and City Boulevard at golden hour.
attractions.where: Best from the Baywalk & City Boulevard
attractions.imageLabel: Drop a Sleeping Dinosaur / Baywalk photo at golden hour

sections.heading: Why go
sections.body: Follow the line of the headland across Pujada Bay and it resolves into a dinosaur lying on its side — Mati's most-photographed silhouette. The City Boulevard and Baywalk are built to enjoy it, especially as the light turns gold in the late afternoon.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Walk the Baywalk, grab something to eat along the Boulevard, and stay for sunset. It pairs naturally with a Pujada Bay trip.

attractions.name: Subangan Museum
attractions.tagline: Davao Oriental's story under one roof
attractions.blurb: The provincial museum in Mati — a place to meet the region's natural history, Mandaya culture, and the story of the coast before you head out to explore it.
attractions.imageLabel: Drop a Subangan Museum photo — gallery / whale skeleton
highlights: A good first stop to understand the region

sections.heading: Why go
sections.body: Subangan — from the Mandaya word for "east", where the sun rises — gathers Davao Oriental's natural history and living culture into one accessible museum. It is the best first stop for understanding the coast, the mountains, and the Mandaya people whose heritage shapes the province.

plan.title: Getting here
plan.body: Fly into Davao City (Francisco Bangoy International). From there, buses and vans run to Mati — roughly 3 to 4 hours by road.

plan.title: Getting around
plan.body: Tricycles and habal-habal cover the city and Dahican. For the islands, book a boat with an accredited operator — check the list before you pay.

plan.title: Where to stay
plan.body: Beach resorts along Dahican, inns and hotels in the city proper. Only accredited establishments are listed.
